result_text:
Template literal contents now count as ignored when JavaScript units are compared for duplication, so the two `greet` functions from your example are reported as one duplicated unit. The full `codeanalyzer` suite passes (330 tests, 0 failures, 3 skipped).

The unit bodies get their literal masking from `extraCleanContent` in `CStyleHeuristicUnitsExtractor`, which handled `"..."` and `'...'` but had no rule for backticks. I added the backtick masking as an override in the JavaScript extractor only, so other languages are unaffected:

- **`codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/lang/js/JavaScriptHeuristicUnitsExtractor.java`**: overrides `extraCleanContent` to first replace each `` `...` `` with ` `` ` and keep its line breaks, then runs the existing cleaning. Masking first means quotes or slashes inside a template can't confuse the other rules. Keeping the line breaks keeps the line mapping intact for multi-line literals.
- **`codeanalyzer/src/test/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/lang/js/JavaScriptHeuristicUnitsExtractorTest.java`** (new): two tests. One checks that the `Hello alpha`/`Hello beta` functions produce a duplicate with both occurrences. The other checks that a code difference outside the literal (`return name + 1`) still keeps them apart.

I did not commit anything.
